solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink juice after eating new biscuit

indicators.note: after says the juice part follows the drink part in the answer

parts.note: brandy is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: eating means the juice word takes the new letter inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink and some juice after munching a fresh biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' is the container signal, not a surface verb about the biscuit; 'after' places the juice part behind the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a thin rolled ginger biscuit, a type of sweet baked treat.

clue.text: Poet recording small stream

indicators.note: recording points to the word as heard on a recording, so a sound-alike

parts.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: A poet records the sound of a babbling stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke was the English poet of the First World War sonnets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was an English poet, famous for The Soldier.

clue.text: Tot was first in a confused state

parts.note: to tot up is to add
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A toddler came first but was muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused, a direct synonym describing a person's state.

clue.text: Time to face up to past requiring treasurer's attention?

definitions.text: Time to face up to past requiring treasurer's attention?

parts.words: Time to face up to past requiring treasurer's attention?
parts.note: a moment when past actions must be answered for, but read as a day when accounts are totted up

explanation.definitionFit: Judgement day, when deeds must be accounted for, is also literally a day for doing sums.

clue.text: Mention of place with dry figure on tour

indicators.note: mention of says the words are spoken, so sound-alikes are wanted

parts.note: a site is a place, and with it goes sere, an old word for dry and withered

explanation.surface: Speaking of a parched place, a tourist turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mention of' turns SITE and SERE into sound-alikes; sere is a literary word for parched.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist visiting landmarks is someone who goes around seeing the sights.

clue.text: Assume trouble before drills

indicators.note: before says the trouble part comes first

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
PT, physical training, is drill exercise

explanation.surface: Take on hardship before going to drills.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a manner or attitude is to take it on, a synonym of assume.

clue.text: Keep firm hold of travel bag

definitions.meaning: an old name for a holdall or small travelling case

explanation.walkthrough: A grip as a travel bag is a somewhat dated British usage for a holdall.
explanation.definitionFit: Grip is both a verb for clutching tightly and a noun for a small holdall, two separate senses.

clue.text: Talk about popular doctor beginning to organise bit of a shower?

indicators.note: about means the talk word goes around the rest

parts.note: rap is slang for talk or chat
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of organise

explanation.surface: A chat about a well-liked doctor starting to plan something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'beginning to' takes just the first letter of organise. The question mark flags that a drop is only part of a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain shower is made up of many falling drops of water.

clue.text: An outstanding corporation?

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch; one that sticks out

explanation.definitionFit: A protruding stomach is humorously called a corporation, and one that stands out is a paunch.

clue.text: Stoical comrade converted leftist

indicators.note: converted suggests the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A stern comrade turned left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of social democracy holds centre-left political views.

clue.text: Old theologian left yard in a strange way

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the crossword's usual theologian

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric walked out of the yard behaving peculiarly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for doing something peculiarly or strangely is a direct synonym.

clue.text: One getting crust from studying it?

definitions.text: One getting crust from studying it?

parts.words: One getting crust from studying it?
parts.note: earning one's crust means making a living; this person makes a living by studying the Earth's crust

explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of rocks studies the Earth's crust and earns a living doing so.

clue.text: Exercise equipment separated by European fellow holding record

indicators.note: separated by means the equipment word is split open with the rest put in the gap

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: holding means the record goes inside the European and fellow letters

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A European man with a record breaks up some gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'separated by' are two nested container signals; EP (extended play) is the usual crossword record.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep-fit is a name for physical exercise done to stay healthy, typically classes.

clue.text: Ornament wild Ted smashed

indicators.note: smashed suggests the letters are broken up and put back together differently

explanation.surface: Wild Ted broke the decorative figurine.
explanation.definitionFit: A twiddle can be a decorative flourish or twirl, so an ornament in writing or music.

clue.text: Having damaged goblet, I leave cooking item

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: After breaking a goblet, a kitchen helper is told to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from plants such as sunflower is a staple used in cooking.

clue.text: A tendency about hotel with old recipes proving loathsome

indicators.note: about means the tendency word goes around the hotel, old and recipes letters

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
R stands for recipe, so two of them give RR

explanation.surface: A habit concerning a hotel's old recipes proves disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HORR inside BENT; R is the old prescription abbreviation for recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent inspires disgust and hatred, the same as loathsome.

clue.text: Caught peasant with a lot of fertiliser for plant

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: peat is used to enrich soil

explanation.surface: A captured farmhand with heaps of compost for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the T from PEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a leguminous plant grown for its edible seeds.

clue.text: Named don working whenever required

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are operated on and reshaped

explanation.surface: A specified university lecturer is busy as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: On demand means available as soon as asked for, at any time required.

clue.text: Stuffy beak might benefit from it?

definitions.text: Stuffy beak might benefit from it?

parts.words: Stuffy beak might benefit from it?
parts.note: beak is slang for a nose (and for a magistrate); a blocked nose needs something to blow into

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffy beak' suggests a pompous judge, beak being British slang for a magistrate, but it is a blocked nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth square for blowing the nose helps someone with a cold and blocked nose.

clue.text: Violent criminal with glasses a jinx

parts.note: a hood is a gangster or thug
OO looks like a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: A thug wearing spectacles brings bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a thing or person that brings bad luck, like a curse.

clue.text: Henry's in a painful spot on land

indicators.note: in means the Henry letter goes inside the rest

parts.note: a sore is a painful place on the body
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry has a sore spot on dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside A SORE; 'Henry's' is Henry is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or to the shore, so on dry land rather than at sea.

clue.text: List held by copper before quiet removal of illegal activity

indicators.note: before says the copper part comes ahead of the quiet letter
held by means the list word sits inside the copper symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A policeman holds a list ahead of a quiet crackdown on crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is the container signal and 'before' orders the pieces; list as a verb means to lean, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean-up campaign rids an area of crime or vice, a noun for such removal.

clue.text: Good number keeping a source of notes

indicators.note: keeping means the good and number letters hold the a between them

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good

explanation.surface: A fine tune holds a single musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is the container signal; PI for good comes from pious, a common crossword shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a musical instrument, so something from which notes come.

clue.text: Wild South American place in our view

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
to us means in our opinion

explanation.surface: A South American city strikes us as untamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly and boisterous behaviour is described as wild, a close synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary tool in front of Indian ascetic, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound

parts.words: tool in front of Indian ascetic
parts.note: a plane is a carpenter's tool, placed in front of a Jain, a follower of the ascetic Indian religion of Jainism

explanation.surface: A simple tool sits before an Indian holy man, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns PLANE then JAIN into sound-alikes spelt differently; Jainism is an Indian faith noted for asceticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain Jane is an unremarkable-looking woman, so the phrase serves as an adjective meaning unexceptional.

clue.text: Charter a diocese partly for broadcast

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Granting a charter to a diocese is partly for public broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium of broadcasting, and as a verb to radio is to transmit.

clue.text: Second plan with conclusion up front

indicators.note: the final letter of the plan word is shifted to the front

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A deputy's scheme puts the ending first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with conclusion up front' moves the last A of IDEA to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is an assistant in a duel or boxing, as is a helper or assistant.

clue.text: Test option scribbled in piece of paper

indicators.note: scribbled suggests the letters are jotted down in a jumbled form

explanation.surface: A test choice is jotted on a scrap of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A Post-it note is a small sticky slip of paper for jotting reminders.
